title: Continuing development.
premise: The meeting about protecting learning time has taken the time reserved for learning.
tension: Synergy wants to make development visible and supported. People & Culture needs time to finish a lesson. Operations wants to leave but initially treats finishing the course as just another checkbox.
beats: People asks whether the check-in can finish soon: she still has a lesson to complete.
Synergy presents the learning plan and asks each person to report progress. The discussion consumes the remaining reserved time.
Operations asks whether attendance at the check-in counts. People explains one specific thing she wants to learn, shifting the conversation away from completion metrics.
Synergy recognizes that another framework will not create more time. He cancels the recurring progress check-in and protects the learning block.
After everyone leaves, Synergy closes his draft about a learning culture and opens his own unfinished lesson. The printer quietly delivers the old agenda.
resolution: Synergy gives people time instead of a new reporting task, and accepts the same permission for himself.

opening_dialogue.text: Can we finish in ten minutes? I’ve still got the course.
